Fact.Name: Screener income limit
Fact.Description: A flat $10,000 over 30 days, not adjusted for household size or for which program was selected. Kept as its own derived fact so the Inspect panel can explain the threshold the same way it explains an answer.

Fact.Name: Over the screener income limit
Fact.Description: The prototype's rule was ((householdIncome undefined AND foodAssistance=="no") OR householdIncome <= 10000) routing to eligible.html, else not-eligible.html. Income is only asked on the SNAP path, so the Medicaid-only applicant always passed. The IsComplete guard reproduces that rather than knocking out on a question that was never put.

All short-circuits: because /isOverScreenerIncomeLimit guards on IsComplete(/screenerHouseholdIncome), it reads false — not incomplete — while a SNAP applicant has yet to answer. That is the right answer for the Medicaid-only path, where the question is never put at all, but it would otherwise let the screener congratulate someone before they have told us anything. The outcome alerts gate on this instead.

Fact.Name: May qualify
Fact.Description: The determination the screener reaches. The prototype's not-eligible.html was not a dead end either — it said "we encourage you to continue" and offered a Continue button — which is exactly why this is a warning rather than a hard knockout.
